newsitem.title: FINLAND: RAUMA CEO SAYS WORST OVER FOR TIMBERJACK.
newsitem.headline: RAUMA CEO SAYS WORST OVER FOR TIMBERJACK.

text.p: Finnish engineering group Rauma Oy on Thursday said the worst was over for its Timberjack forest harvester machinery unit, and the order situation was improving.

"Timberjack will pull out of this cycle," Rauma CEO Heikki Hakala told a news conference after Rauma posted a 16 percent rise in January-August group profit, but said profitability at its forest machine business was "well below" last year.
"We expect the intake of (Timberjack) orders to pick up towards the end of the year," Hakala said.

"The biggest dips are now behind us," he said, referring to the unit. Its January-August sales fell 24 percent to 1,354 million markka from 1,791 million markka, and orders fell 37 percent, Rauma said in a statement.
Rauma said group profit before extraordinary items and tax rose to 427 million markka from 369 million in the year-ago period, and it expected full-year group profitability to be good.
Analysts' median forecast had been for a January-August profit of 485 million markka in a 440 to 505 million range.
Hakala said demand for forest machines would fall in 1996 and 1997, but remain at the average level for cyclical swings.
"In our case, the dip has not been very deep because our market coverage is now broader," he said.

Hakala said Rauma's best forest machine markets now appeared to lie outside Europe, especially in the Far East. He said Rauma also expected demand to pick up in North America. "But we've been waiting for that to happen for some time."
Asked whether Rauma was considering divesting Timberjack, Hakala said: "under no circumstances."
